kernels.title: BF16 projections
kernels.summary: Shape-aware Hopper BF16 projection dispatch with accurate router-weight handling and split-major reductions.

source.license: Apache-2.0 with retained attribution for incorporated public kernel work

intro: This workload mixes low-M BF16 GEMMs with a router path whose FP32 weights are represented as BF16 high and low parts. The retained scored source beat SGLang by 1.131876248733277x on the hosted H200 judge.
The campaign improved from a first scored result near 1.1081x, but remained below the provisional 1.7277x leader.
approach: Dispatch uses a pinned Hopper BF16 GEMV path for selected M=1 projections, custom split-K kernels for profitable pooler and sliced-unpooler shapes, and the official SGLang dispatch elsewhere.
The router preserves BF16 high-plus-low weight semantics, accumulates in FP32, uses full-M tiles, and stores partials split-major for contiguous reduction traffic.
lessons: Changing router partials from output-major to split-major removed a measured strided-reduction penalty.
The profitable custom cutovers were narrow: pooler through M=8 and the sliced N=1024 unpooler.
The highest campaign check used a different candidate than the retained scored source, so best check and paired source check are reported separately.
failures: A direct scalar Triton reduction reached only 0.4877x, and a low-split BF16 attempt reached 0.8161x.
Replacing the workspace reduction with FP32 atomics passed correctness but regressed to 1.1134x because contention hurt larger router shapes.
caveats: The retained dispatch is shape-specific and was measured only through the official challenge shape set on a hosted NVIDIA H200.
Rank 1510 of 1746 is a provisional public snapshot, not a final award or leaderboard win.
This fully AI-agent-driven source has not received a comprehensive originality audit and may contain copied or adapted material; inclusion is not a certification of originality.

kernels.title: Attention decode
kernels.summary: Fused Q/K preparation and fixed-query FlashAttention-3 scheduling for paged decode attention.

source.license: Apache-2.0 with retained attribution for incorporated public kernel work

intro: Attention decode has a small preparation boundary around a much larger paged attention reduction. The retained source beat SGLang by 1.151975903562266x while preserving dense visibility, scaled-cache, and live-slot semantics.
The final public snapshot placed the result 1278 of 1379, behind a provisional 3.3389x leader.
approach: One Triton preparation kernel fuses Q/K RMS normalization, optional interleaved RoPE, FP8 query conversion, and scaled K/V cache insertion.
The retained path uses fixed uniform-query shapes where valid and reuses compatible scheduler metadata so FlashAttention-3 avoids an extra prepare step.
lessons: Removing launch and metadata overhead helped verify and sliding-window shapes, while full B16/B32 attention remained dominated by the FlashAttention-3 main kernel.
The fixed-query metadata variant produced the strongest check at 1.1525x and the retained score at 1.1520x.
Several small point-estimate changes had overlapping confidence intervals and were not treated as proven improvements.
failures: The first fused preparation failed compilation because Triton constants were not constexpr, so it has null performance fields in the public ledger.
A correct custom split-KV Triton gather reached only 0.3974x; random page-1 gathers and small matrix tiles did not replace the Hopper-native attention kernel effectively.
caveats: The fixed-query choice depends on the challenge's uniform query lengths and exact cache contract.
The ranking is provisional, and this result did not approach or surpass the public leader.
This fully AI-agent-driven source has not received a comprehensive originality audit and may contain copied or adapted material; inclusion is not a certification of originality.

kernels.title: Routed experts
kernels.summary: Shape-dependent Marlin routing with fused expert-ID mapping and post-expert normalization and accumulation.

source.license: Apache-2.0 with retained attribution for incorporated public kernel work

intro: The routed-expert problem combines top-8 routing over 256 global experts with NVFP4 weights and BF16 activations on an EP8 rank. The retained source beat SGLang by 1.3402887683867017x.
It placed 1131 of 1425 in the current provisional snapshot, behind a 2.8438x leader.
approach: The kernel retains the lossless SGLang Marlin repack and chooses block 8 through 16 tokens, then block 16 for larger batches.
A Triton program maps global expert IDs to the local 0-31 range. A fused finalizer performs per-expert RMS normalization, route weighting, and FP32 accumulation.
lessons: Routing, alignment, and finalization changes moved the aggregate from a first scored 1.1673x result to 1.3403x.
After those changes, the two Marlin GEMMs still consumed roughly 94-95% of large-shape GPU time.
Every official scored shape in the retained check exceeded the SGLang baseline.
failures: A persistent Triton SIMT GEMV that decoded canonical NVFP4 directly passed correctness but collapsed to 0.2660x.
Fixed block 32, route materialization, and split W13/W2 block policies regressed part of the shape mix and were rejected.
caveats: Preparation assumes EP8 with local experts 0-31, and the verified timing range ends at 256 routed tokens.
H200 does not provide Blackwell native NVFP4 tensor-core MMA; the implementation dequantizes for supported Hopper compute.

kernels.title: Decoder layer
kernels.summary: Whole-layer fusion around attention preparation, expert routing, tuned Marlin blocks, and normalization boundaries.

source.license: Apache-2.0 with retained attribution for incorporated public kernel work

intro: The whole decoder layer exposes interactions that primitive-only benchmarks miss: attention preparation, paged attention, dense projections, routed experts, and residual normalization share the measured score. The retained source beat SGLang by 1.1855883514963717x.
Its current public position is 1172 of 1299 behind a provisional 2.6144x leader.
approach: The retained source fuses Q/K normalization, RoPE, FP8 query conversion, and cache stores, then preserves the proven attention implementation.
The expert section uses shape-tuned Marlin blocks, a Triton pre-expert RMS normalization, fused global-to-local expert mapping, and the established post-expert boundary.
lessons: Isolated block-size changes raised the measured check from 1.0781x to 1.1343x before boundary fusion added the remaining gain.
The exact scored source's paired check was 1.1627x; a later four-warp check reached 1.1644x but did not exceed the retained scored measurement.
Primitive wins required whole-layer validation because attention dominates long full-context shapes while Marlin dominates sliding and verify shapes.
failures: The first fused candidate failed Triton compilation because a global FP8 constant was not constexpr and therefore has no timing metrics.
Block 8 everywhere, T=256 block 16, and T=32 block 32 each regressed important shapes.
caveats: The last check was accepted before the deadline but finished after close and remained off-board; it is not presented as a scored improvement.
The result is tied to the official H200 shape mix and pinned runtime components, and the rank remains provisional.

kernels.title: Prefill layer
kernels.summary: Excluded historical prefill record: both scored submissions were confirmed as complete unchanged copies of pinned public kernels and were withdrawn.

source.license: Apache-2.0 confirmed verbatim public-source copy with the full upstream NOTICE and applicable MIT notice retained

intro: This problem is excluded from retained result summaries. Both scored prefill submissions were confirmed as verbatim copies of complete pinned public kernels, not merely inspired or independently authored implementations.
The measured judge records remain in the immutable historical ledger, while the active score, check, ranking, and progression fields are null after withdrawal and exclusion.
approach: Job c43f7aba5ae84778 was byte-for-byte identical to the pinned Madhavan113 public submission, and job 23b1cc7e2a6040af was byte-for-byte identical to the pinned team keell0renz public kernel.
The published final submission.py bytes and upstream licenses are retained only as historical source evidence.
lessons: Licensing permission, source attribution, originality, and organizer eligibility are distinct questions.
Hash and correctness verification prove byte identity and measured execution, not authorship.
Later tuning measurements do not convert the unchanged copied scored kernels into authored achievements.
failures: The earlier publication described the final public source as adapted or reused but did not state clearly enough that both scored prefill entries were complete unchanged copies.
That presentation has been corrected: both scored jobs are withdrawn and the problem is excluded from active performance summaries.
caveats: No claim is made that organizers issued a ban, disqualification, originality ruling, or eligibility approval.
This public correction addresses organizers and readers but does not claim that a private organizer message was sent.
